summary.title: uiCA: Accurate Throughput Prediction of Basic Blocks on Recent Intel Microarchitectures
summary.one_liner: You learn how a simulation-based pipeline model can predict basic-block throughput on Intel Core CPUs (2011–2021) within about 1% of measured results, and why front-end details matter.
keywords: how accurate are cpu performance models
takeaways: A very simple analytical throughput model is already competitive with existing state-of-the-art predictors, suggesting room for improvement.
uiCA is a detailed parametric pipeline simulator covering Intel Core generations released 2011–2021.
On an improved BHive benchmark, its predictions are usually within 1% of hardware measurements, roughly an order of magnitude better than prior models (per the paper).
Microarchitectural details often considered minor, such as front-end components, are essential for accurate prediction.
The predictor is open source at github.com/andreas-abel/uiCA.
summary.summary: The paper examines how accurate static throughput predictors for basic blocks are, citing prior tools such as IACA, Ithemal, llvm-mca, OSACA and CQA with average errors of 9% to 36%. The authors first build an extremely simple analytical model as a baseline, which turns out to be competitive with the state of the art. They then develop uiCA, a simulation-based predictor built on a detailed parametric pipeline model for Intel Core microarchitectures from 2011 to 2021. It is evaluated on an improved BHive benchmark suite, where predictions are usually within 1% of measured results. The authors report that front-end details such as the predecoder, decoders, micro-op cache and loop buffer are important for accuracy.
